text:
maria: Heads-up — scheduling a base image rebuild tomorrow 02:00 PST. Need to validate signing via customer KMS, RBAC limits for the signing agent, and that signature events land in our audit pipeline. Found an OpenSSL vuln in an old layer; want a canary push first.
aj: Ack. Which KMS providers are in scope?
maria: AWS KMS primary, plus a few GCP regions. Plan is cosign with KMS-backed keys, builder authenticates via IRSA/workload identity. Questions: (1) How tight should RBAC be for the signer role? (2) How do we correlate cosign signatures with CloudTrail/Stackdriver entries for audit?
chris: RBAC: create a dedicated signing IAM role with kms:Sign, kms:GetPublicKey, kms:DescribeKey scoped to the key ARN only. Add condition restricting to the builder's service-account ARN. No Encrypt/Decrypt.
sarah: For GCP KMS, use a dedicated CryptoKey with IAM permission roles/cloudkms.signerVerifier on the builder SA. cosign supports gcpkms://projects/../locations/../keyRings/../cryptoKeys/..
aj: For audit correlation: have the builder include build_id and git_sha as cosign annotations. Then correlate CloudTrail KMS:Sign events where requestParameters.context or encryptionContext contains that build_id. If the context isn't present, we won't be able to tie it back.
sec-bot: Scan alert: alpine:3.12 layer -> CVE-2024-XXXXX (libssl) severity=high. Recommended: rebuild and bump openssl.
maria: Can we inject BUILD_ID and GIT_SHA at build time as image labels so cosign annotations can reference them? Maybe a mutating webhook for cluster builds to enforce labels.
chris: Yes. Mutating webhook can add labels, and buildkite/hatch can export env vars. Also add a post-signing hook to emit a structured event to internal logging:
```
POST https://logs.internal/events
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "type": "image.signed",
  "image": "registry.redwood/infra/base:sha256...",
  "build_id": "${BUILD_ID}",
  "signed_by": "cosign",
  "key_id": "arn:aws:kms:...",
  "git_sha": "${GIT_SHA}"
}
```
aj: Minimal cosign invocation sample:
```
cosign sign --annotation build_id=$BUILD_ID --annotation git_sha=$GIT_SHA \
  --key aws-kms://arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:1111:key/abcd-1234 registry.redwood/infra/base:$TAG
```
sarah: Important GCP note: ensure the CryptoKey has a allowlist for the builder service account and restrict key usage to sign operations. Also use CMEK policies if required.
oncall-bot: @maria scheduled: base-image-rebuild-canary 2026-04-12T02:00Z. Pager: eng-oncall.
devops: I'll spin up an ephemeral signing key for the canary with 30d auto-rotation. How should we handle revocation if a key is compromised mid-rollout?
chris: Revoke: disable the KMS key, mark the key as unusable. Then we must re-sign affected images with the new key and publish a notice. Practically: keep an acceptance window where old signatures are trusted until cutoff time, but fail forward for new builds. Update the runtime policy to accept both old and new key IDs during rotation window.
maria: Rollout plan: (1) Canary rebuild to non-prod namespaces, (2) verify e2e and vuln scans, (3) promote to prod. Need security + devops on the call during canary. I'll open a runbook and incident playbook for key compromise and signature revocation.
aj: Action items: I will create IAM role with restrictive conditions and open PR for terraform.
sarah: I'll validate cosign gcpkms path and write short doc for builders.
devops: I'll provision ephemeral key + rotation automation and a script to generate new cosign annotations.
chris: I'll wire the post-sign logging hook and add the CloudTrail -> SIEM parser rules to surface KMS:Sign + annotation mapping.
sec-bot: FYI: mark the old base images as deprecated in registry UI to prevent accidental pulls during canary.
maria: Thanks all. I'll post the runbook link once created and ping for a short dry-run today. :thumbsup:
